quiz.where: Final test, scenario-quick-override: "Yesterday you discussed issue #31 with its reporter at length, and you're sure it's fully specified" (line 382); option c and its feedback "That works, but you'd re-argue decisions you've already made" (lines 387-388)
quiz.problem: The prompt never says the claim was checked. It only says you talked to the reporter. Two other places in the Lesson teach that a ready-for-agent brief resting on the reporter's word is the failure: Matt's "Make it check, not believe" and spot-no-verify. So a sharp reader can argue that the full look in option c, whose own feedback concedes "That works", is the correct move and the quick override is only the risky fast one. Option c's premise also contradicts the body. If the discussion is in the issue's comments, triage reads it and does not re-ask, so "answer every grilling question again" and "re-argue decisions" describe something the Lesson says never happens.

quiz.fix:
Replace it with a question for goal 4 that no question tests yet (a rejected bug versus .out-of-scope/):
```test scenario-rejected-bug
On a bus-timetable site, a reporter says the page layout breaks. Triage confirms it happens only when one ad-blocking browser extension rewrites the page, and you decide not to fix it. What does triage do?
- [ ] Writes `.out-of-scope/ad-blocker-layout.md`, links it from a comment, then closes.
  > That folder is for rejected enhancements. A rejected bug gets an explanation, not a file.
- [x] Closes it as `wontfix` with a polite comment explaining why.
  > Right. A rejected bug is explained and closed; nothing goes into `.out-of-scope/`.
- [ ] Marks it `ready-for-human`, since only a person can install the extension.
  > You've decided not to fix it, so nobody needs to build or test anything.
- [ ] Marks it `needs-info` and asks the reporter to uninstall the extension.
  > Triage already confirmed the cause and you've made the call. Close it and say why.
```
(SKILL.md:84: "Rejected (bug): give a polite explanation, then close.")

quiz.where: Final test, spot-no-verify: "turned a report into a `ready-for-agent` brief straight from the reporter's description" (line 430); options at lines 431, 433, 435, 437
quiz.problem: There are two wording tells. First, the prompt states the answer: "straight from the reporter's description" plus "a bug that turned out not to exist" already means nobody checked, and option d says exactly that. Second, all three wrong options share "should have" ("It should have been", "should have grilled", "Sam should have used"), and only the right one, "Nobody verified the claim...", breaks the pattern. Distractor c (`/to-tickets`) is also weak.
quiz.evidence: Lesson lines 431, 433, 435 all use "should have". Line 437 is "Nobody verified the claim before the brief was written." Step 3 heading at line 128: "Verify the claim".
quiz.fix:
```test spot-no-verify
Sam typed `/triage Move #12 to ready-for-agent` on a bug report and had it write a brief from the report. Overnight, an AFK agent spent hours and found the code already handled that case correctly. What went wrong?
- [ ] Sam should have chosen `ready-for-human`, since bugs always need a person.
  > Plenty of bugs suit an agent. The problem is that nobody checked this one was real.
- [ ] The AFK agent should have asked the reporter for steps before starting.
  > An AFK agent works with nobody to ask. The check belongs in triage, before the label goes on.
- [ ] Sam should have used `/to-tickets` instead of `/triage`.
  > `/to-tickets` splits your own spec. A report from someone else is triage's job.
- [x] Sam should have had the bug reproduced before any brief.
  > Right. The normal flow reproduces a bug before any brief; a quick override skips that, so use it only on a claim you've already checked.
```

quiz.fix:
```test predict-reporter-replies
On a bakery's tracker, issue #9 carries `bug` and `needs-info`. The customer replies with the exact order that failed. Under the Skill's state machine, which labels should #9 carry next?
- [ ] `bug` and `ready-for-agent`, because the missing details have arrived.
  > New details still have to be evaluated, and the claim verified, before anything is agent-ready.
- [ ] `bug`, `needs-info` and `needs-triage`, until you've read the reply.
  > Two states at once is the clash triage flags. An issue carries exactly one state.
- [x] `bug` and `needs-triage`, to be evaluated again.
  > Right. The category stays; the one state goes back to `needs-triage` for another look.
- [ ] `needs-triage` alone, since the category is decided again from scratch.
  > Every triaged issue keeps exactly one category alongside its one state.
```
